previousRound.outcome: All six fixed, and the blocking one proven both directions by me on the rendered script rather than on a hand-typed command, which is the standard I set before the push. I rendered this head's installScript through the real renderer, gave six copies their own generation directory and one empty shared BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR, and ran them concurrently. After, at this head: 0 of 6 reached the install failure branch. Before, the same rendered script with the flock and the second call stripped and nothing else changed: 3 of 6 hit 'legion plugins: installing … failed' with bun's ENOENT on both @sjawhar packages. I also confirmed the pieces rather than assuming them — /usr/bin/flock is present in this image, it excludes on a directory as well as on a regular file (a holder blocked a waiter until `timeout 3` killed it, exit 124, for both), and with the binary absent the chain is two `not found` lines, the failure branch and exit 1. The five statement corrections landed: worker_shim.go:82 and plugins.go:92 state the shared rule, the ~400 MB Chromium moved into the shared cache-home term, TestEachRolesAgentIsToldAStateHomeOfItsOwn regained the mount and overlap assertions podsafety.go cites, the three socket sites derive from /legion/scratch/tmp, and operatorpod.go's row no longer names a container an operator's mount cannot reach.

keyFindings.description: The lock has no wait bound, so the fix turns one role's stalled install into the whole pod's. `/usr/bin/flock -- "$cache" /usr/local/bin/bun add …` blocks forever by default, and `legion_install || legion_install` makes each waiter queue twice. Measured here rather than read: with a holder running under flock, a waiter was still blocked when `timeout 3` killed it — exit 124 — on a directory and on a regular file alike. Before this push the six installs ran concurrently and failed or succeeded independently; after it, five roles queue behind the first with no bound, charged to the registration deadline (worker_boot_timeout_seconds 120 x worker_boot_registration_deadline_intervals 3 = 360 s), and a relaunch renders the same script and queues again. The normal case is unaffected — my six-way cold run was 6/6 and seconds long — so this is the tail, but the tail is a pod-wide launch failure under a message that mentions no lock, in exactly the plugin-bump scenario the lock was added for. `flock -w <seconds>` bounds it and exits 1, which falls into the retry and then the named failure branch already there, so the failure stays the one the script reports; the bound wants stating against the 360 s deadline in the comment that already discusses the lock's scope. Neither that comment nor docs/kubernetes.md:1856-1869 currently says the wait is unbounded.

The install now cannot run without `/usr/bin/flock`, and that dependency is declared nowhere the image's other tools are. The apt line installs `ca-certificates chromium curl git jq openssh-client python3 socat wget` — no util-linux — and the `toolchain` capability `legion probe-image` asserts lists 'go, curl, wget, python3, node, bun, uv, kubectl, jq and ssh-keygen' (capabilities.go:96), so neither the build nor the probe would notice its absence. It is present today only because Debian's required set drags util-linux into the base. I traced the failure: with the binary gone the chain is two `not found` lines, the failure branch and exit 1 — so every installing launch fails, everywhere, under a message that blames the install rather than the missing tool. That matters more than it would for a degradable dependency, because the retry alone does not reliably survive the race (the tester's flock-removed, retry-kept control failed 2 of 6 on a cold run), so a silent fallback to retry-only would look fine and be the bug. Name it in both lists.

A rate from one experiment is stated as the race's outcome, and plugins_test.go then transfers it to a scenario nothing measured. plugins.go:104-108 says six concurrent `bun add --backend=copyfile --exact` against one empty cache 'leave one exit 0 and five exit 1', naming no packages; plugins_test.go:32-33 goes further — 'without the lock a bump fails five of six launches, and without the retry an agent's own bun install racing the same cold entry fails one'. The five-of-six split belongs to the chalk/lodash probe, which docs/kubernetes.md:1853-1857 scopes correctly, names its packages and says 'measured twice', and which does reproduce. Every measurement of the rendered pair disagrees: the implementer's 3 of 6, the tester's 4 of 6 then 2 of 6, and my own 3 of 6 today. 'Fails one' has no measurement behind it at all — the tester's control was flock-removed with the retry kept, and gave 2 of 6. Only the failure is reliable; the split is not, and this is the sentence a future reader uses to decide whether the lock still earns its keep. Keep the measured numbers in docs, which already scopes its experiment, and let the code and test comments state the rule and what the test pins.

The one test that executes the rendered script now hard-requires `/usr/bin/flock` by absolute path and inherits the ambient cache. `bunInstallArgs` guards only on `exec.LookPath("sh")`, so on a machine without flock — a developer's Mac, a platform this pull request names twice at worker_shim_test.go:23 and shim_test.go:389 — the script exits 127 and the three callers fail at the second check with 'the script never ran bun', which points at the wrong cause. The package already has the shape for an OS guard at launcher/namespace_test.go:49. Separately the test inherits BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR: unset in CI, so the `${…:-<genDir>}` default is what CI exercises, but set inside a role container, where running the suite mkdirs and takes a real exclusive flock on the issue's shared cache. Pin it under t.TempDir() with cmd.Env and the two environments stop exercising different code.

The cache default cannot fire, and its stated purpose argues against the discipline the rest of the package keeps. `installScript` runs only in a Kubernetes role container — installArgv returns the agent unchanged whenever plugins is nil, which is every tmux launch (plugins.go:160-163) — and there BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR is always set, fenced by runtimeOwned and by TestTheRuntimeTellsTheShimEveryScratchDirectoryItMakes, with EnsureScratch having already made the directory before the shim execs the script. So neither `${BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR:-<genDir>}` nor the `mkdir -p` can do anything in production. The comment says the default exists to keep the script 'from aborting if it is somehow unset' — which is to disable, for this one variable, the `set -u` that would otherwise catch the invariant the package spends a coupling test enforcing. It also puts the script in the position of making a scratch directory in the same push that has worker_shim.go assert nothing else makes them. I asked for the mkdir and stand by it; the default is the part worth reconsidering. Either use the variable directly and let `set -u` abort loudly, or keep the mkdir and drop the default with its paragraph.
